_note: Electrical and Electronics (EEE, ECE, EIE) field. Contains EXACTLY the 43 categories used by the frozen electrical_electronic_engineering records of 24.10.2026 (sums expanded to their parts), nothing else. GPU-R has 66 categories in total across all fields (the 65 record categories + surveying_geodesy, approved 26.10.2026).
_classification_rules: 1. REFERENCE, NOT A LOOKUP TABLE. Decide every course by what it actually teaches (syllabus/unit content when available, otherwise your best reading of the title). Definitions, includes, excludes and typical topics describe each category; example course titles only illustrate it. They come from one Indian university (JNTUH) and are never a list a course must match.

2. NEVER FORCE A COURSE INTO A CATEGORY. If a course's real content does not fit any category in this file, return no category for it. Languages, workshops, constitution, gender/ethics awareness, environmental awareness, internships, seminars and projects normally get no subject category.

3. NEVER INVENT A CATEGORY. Use only the exact category IDs listed in category_evidence_status of THIS file. Never create, rename, merge or split categories, and never use an ID from another field's file. GPU-R has one fixed set of categories for all fields; this file contains the ones this field needs.

4. SEVERAL CATEGORIES ARE NORMAL. A course may get several categories if it really teaches each of them. Just list them; never split, divide or repeat its credits. The engine does all counting (inside one requirement or sum a course counts once; across separate requirements the engine applies the regulation rules).

5. SAME-SUBJECT RULES (_implies) are applied automatically after you classify: a course in the first category is also placed in the implied one. They describe one subject with two names, or a part of a larger category.

6. SUMS ARE COMPUTED, NOT ASSIGNED. aggregate_categories and contextual_categories (e.g. general_mathematics, general_cs) are calculated by the engine from the categories you assign. Never assign a sum ID to a course.
7. LABS follow their theory course: a lab gets the categories of the subject it practises.
8. When unsure between categories, use the excludes lines: they say where a topic belongs instead.

9. MIXED COURSES. Many courses teach two subjects. Look at the units: every category that makes up a substantial, dedicated part of the content (as a guide, at least 40% of the units) is assigned. Typical mixed courses: Data Mining (data analysis + machine learning), Compiler Design (programming + theoretical CS), Analog and Digital Electronics (electronics + digital systems), Computer Networks (networks, and computer engineering by rule S3). Do not drop a category just because the course title names only one subject.
_architecture: ATOMIC categories (the LLM assigns these) + AGGREGATE / CONTEXTUAL sums (the engine computes these). A course may carry several atomic categories.
_aggregation_method: UNION of unique course-instance credits, NOT sum of category totals. A single dual-mapped course's credits are counted once per aggregate, never double-counted.

_evidence_status_definitions.VERIFIED: Credits confirmed via actual syllabus/module handbook content, not just course title. May be used for automatic hard-requirement matching.
_evidence_status_definitions.SUPPORTED_BY_TITLE: Course title strongly suggests this category, based on official curriculum documents. Provisional -- do not use alone for hard rejection of a program requirement; treat as a strong candidate pending confirmation.
_evidence_status_definitions.REQUIRES_SYLLABUS_VERIFICATION: No confident title-based match found, but this does not establish the student lacks qualifying coursework. Request module handbook/study regulation before concluding ineligibility.
_evidence_status_definitions.NO_EVIDENCE: Reserved for cases where transcript and verified curriculum evidence together genuinely establish no qualifying coursework exists. Not currently used anywhere in this taxonomy -- we have not reached this level of certainty for any category.

_matching_engine_rule: PASS: category total (VERIFIED credits only, or SUPPORTED_BY_TITLE if the program allows provisional matching) meets or exceeds the requirement. FAIL: only when NO_EVIDENCE status applies AND the requirement is unmet -- this state is not currently used in this taxonomy. NEEDS_VERIFICATION: SUPPORTED_BY_TITLE or REQUIRES_SYLLABUS_VERIFICATION credits are insufficient alone to meet a requirement -- request additional evidence before rejecting the student. Never silently convert REQUIRES_SYLLABUS_VERIFICATION into a 0-credit assumption.
